+# Acceptance Criteria
+
+- AC1: A v2 `tree` request with `scope: "graph"` returns, for the root and for any folder, the folders containing indexed files (sorted, with file counts, a module folder carrying its module node) followed by that folder's file nodes (sorted), never symbols; pages of at most 100 entries chain by `nextCursor` to the full child list with no duplicate or missing entry; `scope: "wiki"` returns page-type groups at the root and a group's pages under it. [verify: exec `bun test src/integrations/metaproject-explorer-tree.test.ts`]
+- AC2: Malformed `tree` requests (unknown keys, bad scope, absolute or `..` parent, bad cursor) answer `invalid-input`; an unknown parent answers `not-found`; a cursor or `expectedSnapshotId` from another snapshot answers `stale-snapshot`; `capabilities` lists `tree`; v1 requests parse and answer exactly as before. [verify: exec `bun test src/integrations/metaproject-explorer-tree.test.ts src/integrations/metaproject-explorer.test.ts` · sensitive: failure-scenario]
+- AC3: The Desktop Rust command accepts a well-formed `tree` request, refuses a malformed one, and still requires of a CLI only the six existing actions. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop/src-tauri && cargo test --locked metaproject`]
+- AC4: Desktop learns from the capability probe whether the CLI offers `tree`; against a CLI that does not, the explorer negotiates successfully and the sidebar shows today's flat list with no error. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/platform/metaproject.test.ts src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx` · sensitive: failure-scenario]
+- AC5: The tree component renders folders, groups and node rows with WAI-ARIA tree semantics and roving focus; Up/Down/Left/Right/Home/End/Enter/Space behave as the plan states; expanding reads a folder once and shows a loading row; a failed folder read shows an inline error whose Retry re-reads only that folder; "Show more" appends the next page in order; selecting a node row calls the selection callback with that node; a graph that is not built shows an empty-state line. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx` · sensitive: failure-scenario]
+- AC6: In the explorer, the tree shows without a query and flat results with one; expanded folders and the selection survive leaving and returning to the view and switching between Graph and Wiki; a selection made elsewhere expands its ancestors and scrolls its row into view without moving focus; a new snapshot keeps the expanded set, drops stale children and answers, and never sends an old-snapshot cursor. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC7: The Desktop package type-checks and its whole test suite passes. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit && bun test src`]
+- AC8: The core package lints and type-checks. [verify: exec `bun run lint && bun run typecheck`]
+- AC9: The Desktop Metaproject guide describes the tree (Graph folders, Wiki groups, keyboard, behaviour with an older CLI) and the docs checks pass. [verify: exec `bun run docs:check`]

+# Desktop Metaproject: tree navigation in the sidebar
+
+Status: formalized
+Source: owner request of 2026-11-24 ("look at what is next in the plan, start a flow in a new worktree and implement the next stage"). The tree is the third complaint of the owner's 2026-11-23 review of the Metaproject screen; flow 515 deferred it because it needs a new explorer action and a relaxed capability handshake ([515 description](../515-2026-11-23-desktop-metaproject-graph-panel/description.md), Out of Scope).
+
+## Problem
+
+The left list of the Metaproject screen (`apps/desktop/src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.tsx`, `nav.metaproject-list`) shows, without a search, a flat list of the catalog's first nodes. The catalog is capped at 200 nodes (`METAPROJECT_NODE_LIMIT`), while this repository indexes about 4,600 files, 200 modules and 125 wiki pages. So:
+
+- most of the project cannot be reached from the list without typing a search;
+- the list has no structure: files, modules and wiki pages of every folder are mixed in one column, so the user cannot browse "what is in `src/flow`";
+- the Wiki view lists pages without the grouping the wiki itself uses (architecture, components, business rules, …).
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+- Without a search query, the list is a tree. In **Graph** it mirrors the indexed files by folder: folders first, then files, each folder with the number of indexed files under it; a folder that is a module can be selected as that module's graph node. In **Wiki** pages are grouped by page type.
+- Folders load their children on demand from a new paged Core action, so the whole project is reachable however large it is.
+- The tree is keyboard-operable as a WAI-ARIA tree, keeps its expanded folders when the user leaves the explorer and comes back, and reveals the selected node when the selection changes elsewhere (graph click, search result, Back).
+- With a search query the list stays the current flat result list.
+- A Desktop talking to an older CLI that does not offer the tree action keeps today's flat list, with no error.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- On this repository, every indexed file is reachable from the Graph list without typing a search: the root lists the top-level folders, and expanding them leads to any file (measured by the tree contract tests over a fixture, and by the operator on this checkout).
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Changing what the graph, the details panel or the OpenSpec view show (flows 515 and 514 own them).
+- Read latency and cancellation of explorer reads (about 0.8 s per read; a separate stage).
+- Actions on a tree row beyond selecting it (open in Files, send to a session, start a flow).
+- Drag and drop, renaming, or any write to the project.
+- Native screenshots for the guide.
+- New dependencies.

+# Plan — tree navigation in the Metaproject sidebar
+
+## Approach
+
+One new read-only v2 action, `tree`, returns the children of one tree node, paged. Desktop asks for the root when the list first shows the tree and for a folder's children when the user expands it. The action is optional: a reader lists it in `capabilities`, and Desktop uses the tree only when the answering CLI offers it. Everything else in the explorer is unchanged.
+
+Rejected: sending the whole tree in `catalog` (4,600 files exceed the catalog's 200-node cap and the 1 MiB response bound on larger repos); building the tree client-side from search results (incomplete and slow).
+
+## Contract (Core, `src/integrations/metaproject-explorer-contract.ts`)
+
+Request:
+
+```ts
+{ version: 2; action: "tree"; scope: "graph" | "wiki"; parent?: string; cursor?: string; expectedSnapshotId?: string }
+```
+
+- `scope: "graph"` — `parent` absent is the checkout root; otherwise a checkout-relative folder path (`isMetaprojectRelativePath`). Children: the folders directly under `parent` that contain at least one indexed file node (any depth), sorted by name; then the file nodes directly under `parent`, sorted by name. Symbols never appear. A folder whose path equals a module node's path carries that module node.
+- `scope: "wiki"` — `parent` absent lists one group per wiki page type present (key = the page type, `other` for pages without one), sorted by display name; `parent` = a group key lists that group's pages sorted by title.
+- Exact keys, as every other v2 action; anything else is `invalid-input`. An unknown `parent` is `not-found`. A mismatched `expectedSnapshotId` or a cursor from another snapshot is `stale-snapshot`.
+
+Response:
+
+```ts
+interface MetaprojectTreeV2 {
+  schemaVersion: 2; snapshotId: string;
+  scope: "graph" | "wiki"; parent: string | null;
+  entries: MetaprojectTreeEntry[];
+  nextCursor?: string;   // more entries of this parent
+  partial: boolean;      // the source behind the scope is missing or incomplete
+}
+type MetaprojectTreeEntry =
+  | { type: "folder"; path: string; name: string; files: number; module?: MetaprojectNode }
+  | { type: "group"; key: string; name: string; pages: number }
+  | { type: "node"; node: MetaprojectNode };
+```
+
+Paging: at most `METAPROJECT_PAGE_SIZE_V2` entries and `METAPROJECT_RESPONSE_BYTES_V2` per page, with the existing snapshot-bound cursor helpers. A graph that is not built answers `entries: []`, `partial: true` for `scope: "graph"`; the wiki scope answers from whatever wiki pages the catalog source has. `capabilities` adds `"tree"` to `METAPROJECT_CAPABILITIES`. v1 parsing and responses do not change.
+
+## Transport
+
+- **Rust** (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/metaproject.rs`): add `RequestV2::Tree { scope: TreeScope, parent: Option<String>, cursor: Option<String>, expected_snapshot_id }`, validated in `valid_v2` (graph `parent` a `relative_path`, wiki `parent` `valid_text`, cursor `valid_text`). `ACTIONS` — the set a CLI must offer — stays the six existing actions. Rust tests cover accept and refuse cases. Verified in GitHub CI only (no local cargo).
+- **Desktop platform** (`apps/desktop/src/platform/metaproject.ts`): request/response types for `tree`, a response guard, and the negotiated capability set exposed to the view (for example `supportsTree`), so the view can tell an older CLI from a newer one. The handshake still requires only the actions Desktop always sends.
+- **Dev bridge**: no change expected (it uses `parseExplorerRequest`); confirm with a test or a note.
+
+## Desktop UI
+
+New component `apps/desktop/src/metaproject/MetaprojectTree.tsx` (+ `MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx`), mounted inside `nav.metaproject-list` of `MetaprojectView.tsx` when there is no search query, the mode is Graph or Wiki, and the CLI offers `tree`. Otherwise the list renders exactly as today.
+
+- WAI-ARIA tree: `role="tree"` with an accessible name; rows `role="treeitem"` with `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-expanded` on folders/groups, `aria-selected` on the selected node; one roving `tabIndex=0`. Keys: Up/Down move, Right expands or enters the first child, Left collapses or goes to the parent, Enter/Space selects a node row or toggles a folder, Home/End go to the first/last visible row. Focus is never moved by data arriving.
+- Rows: folder/group = disclosure chevron, name, count; node row = title and the existing kind label; a module folder row selects the module node on Enter/click on its name and toggles on the chevron.
+- Selecting a node row calls the same path a search result uses today (`openHit`/`select`/`openDocument`), so Graph, panel, Wiki and Back behave as they do now.
+- Loading: a folder being read shows one "Loading…" row under it; a failed read shows an inline row with the error and a Retry that re-reads only that folder; a `nextCursor` shows a "Show more" row that appends the next page.
+- State: expanded folders and loaded children are kept per scope (graph, wiki) in the explorer state that already survives leaving the view (flow 515). A new snapshot drops loaded children, keeps the expanded set, re-reads expanded folders, and silently forgets folders that no longer exist.
+- Reveal: when the selection changes from outside the tree (graph click, search result, Back, details panel), the tree expands the selected node's ancestor folders (reading them as needed), scrolls the row into view (`block: "nearest"`) and does not take focus.
+- Heading: `Files` in Graph, `Wiki` in Wiki, with the root counts; search keeps `Results · N`.
+- Styling uses the existing tokens and list classes of `metaproject.css`; no new colours.

 ## Find a page, file, module or symbol
 
+Browse the tree in the list on the left, or search when you know a name.
+
+### Browse the tree
+
+Without a search, the list is a tree:
+
+- In **Graph**, it shows the folders and files of the checkout. The header
+  reads **Files** with the number of indexed files. In each folder, its
+  folders come first, then its files, in name order. Only folders that hold
+  indexed files appear, and each shows how many files it holds, counting its
+  subfolders. A folder that is also a module can be selected as that module:
+  click its name or press **Enter** to select it, and click the chevron or
+  press **Space** to expand or collapse it. Click any other folder to expand
+  or collapse it.
+- In **Wiki**, it groups the pages by page type, such as **Component** or
+  **Domain model** for `domain-model` pages, with the number of pages in each
+  group. Pages without a page type are under **Other**. The header reads
+  **Wiki** with the number of pages.
+
+Click a file or page to select it, as you would a search result. A folder
+loads its contents when you first expand it and shows **Loading…** until
+they arrive. A large folder shows its first entries and a **Show more** row
+that loads the next ones. If a folder fails to load, its row reads **Could
+not load.** with the reason and a **Retry** button.
+
+Use the keyboard once the tree has focus:
+
+| Key | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Up** / **Down** | Move to the previous or next row. |
+| **Home** / **End** | Move to the first or last row. |
+| **Right** | Expand a closed folder or group, or move to its first entry when it is open. |
+| **Left** | Collapse an open folder or group, or move to its parent. |
+| **Enter** | Select a file, page or module folder. On another folder or a group it expands or collapses it. On a **Show more** or **Retry** row it runs that action. |
+| **Space** | Expand or collapse a folder or group, or select a file or page. |
+
+Expanded folders and groups stay open when you leave the Metaproject tab and
+return, and when you switch between **Graph** and **Wiki**. When you select an
+item from somewhere else, such as a node in the graph or a link in an
+article, the tree expands the folders on its path and scrolls to it. The item
+shown when you first open the explorer does not expand the tree.
+
+If the graph is not built, the **Graph** tree reads **The graph is not built
+yet. Rebuild the graph to browse its files.** The **Wiki** tree still works.
+
+The tree needs a Keryx CLI that serves it. With an older CLI, the list stays
+the flat catalog list described below and everything else works as before.
+

 ## Recover from common problems
 
 | What you see | What to do |
 | --- | --- |
 | **Graph missing** | Open existing wiki pages in **Wiki**, or select **Rebuild graph** to add code relationships. |
 | **Graph stale** after switching branches or changing code | Rebuild from the open checkout. The stale graph can still show results from its last build. |
 | **Graph unknown** or a layer fails to load | Rebuild and check the terminal output. For `defines` or `calls`, also check `keryx gdgraph symbols status`. |
 | **Project knowledge changed while loading** | The graph was rebuilt, or a wiki page or OpenSpec file changed, between two reads. Select **Refresh catalog** to load a consistent snapshot. |
 | **Search failed** | Select **Retry search** to repeat the current query. |
+| A tree row reads **Could not load.** | Select **Retry** on that row to read the folder or group again. |
+| The **Graph** tree reads **The graph is not built yet.** | Select **Rebuild graph**, or run `keryx gdgraph build` from the open checkout. |
+| The list shows **Catalog · shown of total** instead of a tree | The selected CLI does not serve the tree. Choose the bundled CLI in **Settings → Desktop**, or update the CLI. Search and the flat list keep working. |
 | The CLI does not support Metaproject Explorer | Choose the bundled CLI in **Settings → Desktop**, or update the CLI and Desktop together. |
 | The selected CLI returned invalid Metaproject capabilities | The CLI lacks a read action this Desktop uses. Choose the bundled CLI in **Settings → Desktop**, or update the CLI. |
 | A page has no **Relationships** section | Confirm the page links to other wiki pages or declares the code it covers, then rebuild the graph and check the filters in **Graph**. |
